content: PanoRef coverage optimizer implementation review: algorithm architecture rated 8/10, search modes 7.5/10, complex imported set readiness 4/10. Strengths include deterministic area-proportional surface sampling, comprehensive origin evaluation (occlusion, normals, viewing angle, texel density, visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, continuous quality), genuinely joint pair mode (evaluates all legal coarse pairs ranked by bitset union with quality/contribution tie-breakers), and a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches). Six blockers identified: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because candidate clearance uses object AABB distance with 0.3m rejection threshold—points inside AABB get zero clearance and are rejected, affecting single-GLB imports, combined room shells/furniture, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, and large models with empty interior; fix requires actual geometry clearance via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast, with per-connected-mesh or spatial-cluster obstacle bounds and a regression test. (2) Geometry representation won't scale to heavy imports—every triangle expanded to three independent Vec3 arrays plus normals, IDs, area; for 3M triangles minimum packed data is ~144MB (positions 108MB + normals 36MB) but actual JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers are several times larger, structured-cloned to worker via postMessage creating another enormous representation, BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays, and every triangle intersection allocates temporary 3-element arrays causing extreme GC pressure; fix uses compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions, Uint32Array indices, optional Float32Array normals, Uint32Array meshRanges, Float32Array transforms), transfers ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects, and uses three-mesh-bvh, flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries while avoiding expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle. (3) Geometry extraction blocks main thread—panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene before creating/posting to worker, so worker keeps expensive optimizer off UI thread but not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, or structured cloning; on complex models app may freeze before worker reports first progress; fix moves extraction into worker or chunks/yields between meshes. (4) 'Apply to selected panorama pair' is conceptually wrong—UI allows optimized origins written directly into two existing panorama references via updatePanoReference changing stored origins, but existing panorama was rendered/captured from original origin so changing metadata doesn't transform image, merely projects old pixels from wrong point ruining alignment; correct workflow for fixed-first preserves existing panorama and origin, moves next capture origin to B, renders new graybox panorama, inpaints/generates new styled panorama, imports as secondary; for joint mode creates two-origin capture plan, moves to A, captures/renders A, moves to B, captures/renders B, associates each imported result with actual origin; existing panorama origins must remain immutable. (5) Reachable upper bound mathematically inconsistent—reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates while final combined coverage uses different fine sample bank generated with seed+1, so UI can show Combined coverage 83%, Reachable upper bound 80%, Reachable captured 100%; clamp hides impossible ratio but doesn't repair incompatible estimates; also fixed-first reachable set calculated before arbitrary first origin evaluated so fixed first origin not included in reachable upper bound at all; fix uses common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and for fixed-first includes fixed origin in reachable union. (6) Fixed-first doesn't enforce minimum separation—joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation but fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity not position/distance, so even identical candidate position survives since first evaluation is separate object; add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation. Important refinements: 'four-level refinement' not truly iterative—offsets generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16) without selecting best half-step result and centering quarter-step search around new result, so it's useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not coordinate/pattern refinement described in plan; local candidates can float between floors—candidate validation only checks whether floor exists somewhere below candidate, local offsets retain original Y coordinate, on sloped terrain or multilevel sets offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height leaving panorama origin floating meters above new floor, fix for each offset finds floor under new X/Z, sets Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then performs clearance; optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules—optimizer evaluates angle and texel density but actual shader blends both panoramas only by distance when visible, so optimizer may prefer source for frontal angle while runtime favors closer but more grazing source, shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Testing assessment: current tests good unit tests but most dangerous cases absent—(1) one large imported object containing entire room, (2) 100k+ triangle performance fixture, (3) reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, (4) fixed-first candidate separation, (5) sloped and multilevel floors, (6) existing panorama origins remaining immutable, (7) candidate generation inside concave imported geometry; no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head so reported test suite not independently enforced in CI. Recent work: rebased onto main and resolved PR conflict; added allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering; ran one real complex imported-set benchmark and added full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not merely BVH-construction test); removed stale test guarding old distance-only blend heuristic, removed dead shader constant PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0, replaced assertion protecting new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0), targeted regression passes (36 tests in multiOriginInteraction.test.ts); full test suite 42 test files, 371 tests passed, lint (tsc --noEmit) passed, build (vite build) passed producing 1777 modules transformed; coverage.worker asset 98.15 kB; projectionCoverage.test.ts runs both complete optimizer modes on 100k+ triangle indexed fixture (39235ms); projectedStyleCompile.test.ts compiles projected materials under real WebGL with single and dual projector modes (3934ms); projectedReceive.test.ts receiving projected-style material single-projector not blended 50/50, rears fall back, modes differ (4309ms); occlusionPixel.test.ts radial-depth occlusion cubemap real WebGL pixel readback generates valid depth cubemap front hit opposite no-hit clear depth packed (3973ms). Goal: accomplish above and spawn subagent to disprove goal fully complete, report lacking items, fix, repeat until subagent unable to find holes.
